title: The North Atlantic Treaty (1949)
summary: Founding treaty establishing NATO and collective self-defense obligations under Article 5.
content: The Parties to this Treaty reaffirm their faith in the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations and their desire to live in peace with all peoples and all governments. They are determined to safeguard the freedom, common heritage and civilisation of their peoples, founded on the principles of democracy, individual liberty and the rule of law. They seek to promote stability and well-being in the North Atlantic area. They are resolved to unite their efforts for collective defence and for the preservation of peace and security. Article 5: The Parties agree that an armed attack against one or more of them in Europe or North America shall be considered an attack against them all and consequently they agree that, if such an armed attack occurs, each of them, in exercise of the right of individual or collective self-defence recognised by Article 51 of the Charter of the United Nations, will assist the Party or Parties so attacked by taking forthwith, individually and in concert with the other Parties, such action as it deems necessary, including the use of armed force, to restore and maintain the security of the North Atlantic area. Article 6 defines the territory covered by Article 5, including the territory of any of the Parties in Europe or North America, Algerian Departments of France, Turkey, or islands under the jurisdiction of any Party in the North Atlantic area north of the Tropic of Cancer.

title: UNCLOS Part III: Straits Used for International Navigation
source_name: United Nations Division for Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea
summary: UN Convention on the Law of the Sea governing transit passage through international straits.
content: Article 37 of UNCLOS specifies that this section applies to straits which are used for international navigation between one part of the high seas or an exclusive economic zone and another part of the high seas or an exclusive economic zone. Article 38 defines the Right of Transit Passage: In straits referred to in article 37, all ships and aircraft enjoy the right of transit passage, which shall not be impeded; transit passage means the exercise in accordance with this Part of the freedom of navigation and overflight solely for the purpose of continuous and expeditious transit of the strait. Ships and aircraft, while exercising the right of transit passage, shall proceed without delay through or over the strait, refrain from any threat or use of force against the sovereignty, territorial integrity or political independence of States bordering the strait, and comply with generally accepted international safety regulations at sea. States bordering straits shall not hamper transit passage and shall give appropriate publicity to any danger to navigation or overflight within or over the strait of which they have knowledge. There shall be no suspension of transit passage.

title: Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits (1936)
source_name: League of Nations Treaty Series (United Nations Treaty Collection)
summary: International convention establishing Turkey's sovereignty and maritime regulation over the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits.
content: The Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits regulates maritime traffic through the Turkish Straits (the Bosporus and Dardanelles) and the Sea of Marmara. Under the convention, merchant vessels enjoy freedom of transit and navigation in the Straits in time of peace under any flag and with any kind of cargo, without formalities other than sanitary inspections and dues. In time of war, Turkey not being belligerent, warships of non-belligerent Powers enjoy freedom of transit under the conditions laid down in the convention; however, warships belonging to belligerent Powers shall not pass through the Straits, except in cases of assistance rendered to a State victim of aggression in accordance with pacts binding Turkey. Article 19 states that in time of war, warships of belligerent Powers cannot pass through the Straits, with an exception for warships belonging to belligerent Powers which have become separated from their home bases, allowing them to return to their home ports. In time of war, Turkey being belligerent, or considering herself threatened with imminent danger of war, the passage of warships is left entirely to the discretion of the Turkish Government.

title: Taiwan Relations Act (Public Law 96-8)
summary: US law defining commercial, cultural, and security relations with Taiwan following normalization of relations with the PRC.
content: The Taiwan Relations Act (TRA) declares it to be the policy of the United States to preserve and promote extensive, close, and friendly commercial, cultural, and other relations between the people of the United States and the people on Taiwan. The Act states that peace and stability in the Western Pacific area are in the political, security, and economic interests of the United States and are matters of international concern. It explicitly states that the United States decision to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China rests upon the expectation that the future of Taiwan will be determined by peaceful means. The Act considers any effort to determine the future of Taiwan by other than peaceful means, including by boycotts or embargoes, a threat to the peace and security of the Western Pacific area and of grave concern to the United States. It directs the United States to make available to Taiwan such defense articles and defense services in such quantity as may be necessary to enable Taiwan to maintain a sufficient self-defense capability, and to maintain the capacity of the United States to resist any resort to force or other forms of coercion that would jeopardize the security, or the social or economic system, of the people on Taiwan.

title: Joint Leaders Statement on AUKUS Enhanced Trilateral Security Partnership
source_name: The White House / UK Cabinet Office / Australian Government
summary: Trilateral security partnership between Australia, the UK, and the US focusing on nuclear-powered submarines and advanced capabilities.
content: On September 15, 2021, the leaders of Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States announced the creation of an enhanced trilateral security partnership called AUKUS. AUKUS is designed to deepen diplomatic, security, and defense cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region. The partnership consists of two key pillars: Pillar 1 centers on supporting Australia in acquiring conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines (SSN-AUKUS) for the Royal Australian Navy, fully respecting the highest non-proliferation standards and working in close partnership with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Pillar 2 focuses on trilateral collaboration across advanced military technologies and joint capabilities, including artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, undersea capabilities, hypersonic and counter-hypersonic systems, electronic warfare, and cyber defense. The initiative emphasizes interoperability and collective deterrence in response to evolving geopolitical competition across the Indo-Pacific.

title: United Nations Security Council Resolution 2231 on Iran Nuclear Agreement (JCPOA)
summary: UN Security Council endorsement of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) concerning Iran's nuclear program and sanctions relief.

title: Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation between India and the USSR (1971)
source_name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
summary: Foundational bilateral treaty establishing mutual consultations and defense deterrence between New Delhi and Moscow.
content: Signed in New Delhi on August 9, 1971, by Indian Foreign Minister Swaran Singh and Soviet Foreign Minister Andrei Gromyko. Article VIII specifies that each High Contracting Party solemnly declares that it shall not enter into or participate in any military alliance directed against the other Party. Article IX establishes that each High Contracting Party undertakes to abstain from providing any assistance to any third party that engages in armed conflict against the other Party. In the event of either Party being subjected to an attack or a threat thereof, the High Contracting Parties shall immediately enter into mutual consultations in order to remove such threat and to take appropriate effective measures to ensure peace and security. The treaty provided crucial geopolitical and military deterrence against outside intervention during the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War and cemented long-term defense, scientific, and strategic cooperation.

title: Declaration on Strategic Partnership between the Republic of India and the Russian Federation (2000)
source_name: Ministry of External Affairs, India & Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Russia
summary: Elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, institutionalizing annual leadership summits, defense co-development, and energy cooperation.
content: Signed by Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Russian President Vladimir Putin in New Delhi on October 5, 2000. The declaration institutionalized Annual Bilateral Summits alternating between New Delhi and Moscow, establishing an enduring framework for bilateral relations across political, defense, energy, science, and cultural spheres. Later elevated in December 2010 to a 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership', the framework encompasses joint research and development of defense equipment (such as the BrahMos missile program, licensed production of Su-30MKI, T-90 tanks), long-term hydrocarbons and energy supplies, civilian nuclear energy collaboration at the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, and coordination in multilateral forums including the UN Security Council, BRICS, and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).
